title: Springfield/Merrill Lynch Scandal-Only Little Guy Takes Fall
description: 03/19/08, from 22WWLP in Springfield, MA- Springfield Treasurer Salvatore Calvanese speaks about being told that his boss Stephen Lisauskas had a relationship with the representative from one of the investment firms (Merrill Lynch) they were considering for a city investment.    After the "safe" investments crashed in months, Calvanese has admitted regret and is on leave.  His boss, Lisauskas, who steered over $100 million in business to his friend at Merrill Lynch, continues to run the city and admit nothing.

asr.full_text: Springfield's Treasurer collector, Salveador Calvinis said he warned his superiors when the City's Merrill Lynch investments started going south as 22 News reporter, Jacquelyn Cashmann, discovered during a phone interview with Calvinis he accepts some blame, but says there were others involved Springfield City Hall was shocked to find out their Merrill Lynch investments lost close to $14 million in December 22 News asked City Treasurer, Salvador Calanice. Why Springfield invested money with Meryl Lynch out of Albany New York? Calanice says he was told that then Deputy Director of the finance control board, Stephen Lozowskis had a relationship with a Merrillch broker calvin he says trouble began in february two thousand seven when meryl lynch investors asked him to sign a document which would allow the city's investments to make more money and then they said again he needed to find a document to get you into a higher money market for what can local cnoe one back to work to the fact that we find effects back I can't locate it. No, you'll want to fax it over to me. They faxed it to me, and signed it and faxed it back. You signed it? Yeah. Did you read it? I kind of glanced over it. To just glance at a document and just sign it? Is that – do you wish you didn't do that now? Absolutely. Kalvany says signing the document did contribute to the city losing money, but claims there were other factors. In August, Kalvany says he learned a he learned an investment lost 25% of its value, so when state aid money came he took that 50 million dollars to UBS, not Merrill Lynch. I contacted the executive director. I told them I called T-Bank North, UBS, and Morgan Stanley. The best rate I got was UBS. He asked me why he did not contact Merrill Lynch, and I responded by saying, well, obviously they don't know how to invest our money in, plus why would we give them more funds as a reward? He said, well, you can't really screw up a money marker. Give them a call and see what their rate is. I called them. Their rate was higher than UPS, so the money went to Merrill. Calvin East tells 22 News it wasn't until the 2007 audit that the Merrill Lynch losses became public. Merrill Lynch has since reimbursed the city, acknowledging the investments were not properly authorized. Calvin East is on a medical leave due to the stress of this situation jacklin has mint twenty two news
